notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: LOOP trains interactive digital agents with reinforcement learning in stateful, multi-app environments where tasks are performed through API calls.

name: Advancing Autonomous VLM Agents via Variational Subgoal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses variational subgoal-conditioned reinforcement learning to improve learning efficiency on sparse-reward mobile and web-control tasks.

name: Advancing Language Multi-Agent Learning with Credit Re-Assignment for Interactive Environment Generalization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces CollabUIAgents, a multi-agent RL framework that assigns LLM-based process rewards to help agents generalize across interactive settings including mobile operations and web browsing.

name: Digi-Q: Learning Q-Value Functions for Training Device-Control Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Learns action-value functions from offline device-control experience and uses them to rank candidate actions for policy improvement.

name: VEM: Environment-Free Exploration for Training GUI Agent with Value Environment Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains GUI agents with a frozen value model learned from offline interactions, guiding action exploration without predicting complete next observations.

name: STEVE: A Step Verification Pipeline for Computer-use Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Labels individual computer-use actions by comparing surrounding screenshots, then trains agents from both successful and unsuccessful steps.

name: UI-R1: Enhancing Efficient Action Prediction of GUI Agents by Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses rule-based action rewards and policy optimization to train GUI action prediction from a compact set of mobile tasks.

name: GUI-R1 : A Generalist R1-Style Vision-Language Action Model For GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Applies reinforcement fine-tuning with unified action rules and curated cross-platform examples to vision-language GUI agents.

name: InfiGUI-R1: Advancing Multimodal GUI Agents from Reactive Actors to Deliberative Reasoners
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses a staged reasoning-focused training framework to move GUI agents from reactive actions toward deliberative planning and recovery.

name: A Survey on GUI Agents with Foundation Models Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning
summary: Formalizes GUI tasks as Markov decision processes and traces agent training from prompting through supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning.

name: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). WebShop is one of several agent benchmarks used to evaluate the general training method.
summary: Introduces Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO), an RL method for assigning step-level credit in multi-turn agents, evaluated on WebShop among other tasks.

name: MobileIPL: Enhancing Mobile Agents Thinking Process via Iterative Preference Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileIPL samples trees of action-planning thoughts, propagates rule-based leaf rewards backward, and forms preference pairs for reasoning-level optimization. It also expands screenshot-based instruction data through staged evolution before evaluation on mobile GUI-agent benchmarks.

name: Enhancing Visual Grounding for GUI Agents via Self-Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes GUI grounding training that combines curated seed examples, continuous location-dependent policy feedback, and iterative refinement guided by attention maps. The study evaluates the resulting reinforcement-learning procedure on three grounding benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: GUI-Shift: Enhancing VLM-Based GUI Agents through Self-supervised Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-Shift trains an inverse-dynamics task that predicts the initial action connecting two GUI states, using trajectories without natural-language instructions. It combines rule-based reinforcement learning with data filtering and evaluates transfer to Android automation and screenshot grounding.

name: ReGUIDE: Data Efficient GUI Grounding via Spatial Reasoning and Search
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines self-generated localization reasoning, spatial consistency checks, and inference-time search to improve data-efficient web grounding.

name: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Web-Shepherd is a process reward model for assessing individual steps of web-navigation trajectories. It introduces a collection of 40,000 step-level preference pairs with checklists and a separate benchmark for comparing reward models, then evaluates verification during WebArena-lite navigation.

name: GUI-G1: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Analyzes reasoning templates, reward design, and policy updates in GUI grounding, then proposes targeted adjustments to the training process.

name: ARPO:End-to-End Policy Optimization for GUI Agents with Experience Replay
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ARPO extends group-relative policy optimization with a replay buffer that reuses successful GUI trajectories across training iterations. It filters tasks using baseline performance and compares end-to-end reinforcement learning with offline preference optimization on OSWorld.

name: WebAgent-R1: Training Web Agents via End-to-End Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains web agents through asynchronous multi-turn environment interaction, using task-success rewards to optimize complete trajectories.

name: ProgRM: Build Better GUI Agents with Progress Rewards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ProgRM predicts per-step task completion progress to provide intermediate rewards during online GUI-agent training. It derives progress labels by using longest common subsequences to identify key trajectory steps, allowing useful partial progress to contribute even when a trajectory ultimately fails.

name: ScreenExplorer: Training a Vision-Language Model for Diverse Exploration in Open GUI World
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Trains ScreenExplorer with reinforcement learning in dynamic GUI environments, using a world-model curiosity reward and experience-stream distillation to support sustained exploration.

name: SPA-RL: Reinforcing LLM Agents via Stepwise Progress Attribution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Webshop is evaluated alongside ALFWorld and VirtualHome; the method is presented for general agents.
summary: Introduces SPA, a reward redistribution method for multi-step LLM agents that estimates each action’s contribution to task completion; Webshop is among its evaluations.

name: UI-Genie: A Self-Improving Approach for Iteratively Boosting MLLM-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. Its data pipeline uses rule-based verification, corrupted trajectories, and hard negatives to support reward-guided exploration and iterative training.

name: WorkForceAgent-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLM-based Web Agents via Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses rule-based rewards for output structure and action correctness to train reasoning for enterprise web navigation.

name: Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Visual Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). GUI localization is one part of a broader visual reasoning evaluation.
summary: Introduces ViGoRL, a visual reasoning model trained to reference image coordinates and zoom during reasoning; its evaluations include GUI element localization.

name: ZeroGUI: Automating Online GUI Learning at Zero Human Cost
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines generated tasks, estimated success rewards, and online reinforcement learning to automate GUI-agent interaction training.

name: Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Test-Time Interaction scales the interaction horizon so web agents can explore, backtrack and revise plans within a rollout. Its online reinforcement-learning curriculum adjusts rollout lengths and is evaluated on WebVoyager and WebArena.

name: LPO: Towards Accurate GUI Agent Interaction via Location Preference Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Learning, Reasoning, Refinement: A Framework for Kahneman's Dual-System Intelligence in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CogniGUI combines hierarchical visual parsing of interface elements with a GRPO-based grounding agent that compares alternative interaction paths. Its ScreenSeek benchmark evaluates navigation across applications, changing interface states, and consistency between interfaces.

name: Mobile-R1: Towards Interactive Capability for VLM-Based Mobile Agent via Systematic Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses a staged curriculum from response-format alignment through action feedback to interactive task-level training for mobile agents.

name: GLM-4.5V and GLM-4.1V-Thinking: Towards Versatile Multimodal Reasoning with Scalable Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v6). GUI agents are one task area in a general multimodal model evaluation.
summary: Reports the GLM-4.1V-Thinking, GLM-4.5V, and GLM-4.6V vision-language model family and curriculum-based RL training, with GUI agents among its evaluated tasks.

name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.

name: MobileGUI-RL: Advancing Mobile GUI Agent through Reinforcement Learning in Online Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileGUI-RL constructs an online training curriculum through agent exploration and task filtering. It adapts GRPO with trajectory-aware advantages and rewards for task completion and execution efficiency, evaluated on three online mobile-agent benchmarks.

name: GTA1: GUI Test-time Scaling Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GTA1 samples multiple action proposals at each GUI step and uses a judge to select among them. A separate grounding model is trained with reinforcement learning to map selected proposals to visual targets, linking planning-time search with click localization.

name: GUI-G$^2$: Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-G2 replaces binary grounding rewards with Gaussian point rewards and spatial-coverage rewards. An adaptive variance tied to element dimensions supplies continuous training feedback for targets of different sizes, evaluated on the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

name: UI-AGILE: Advancing GUI Agents with Effective Reinforcement Learning and Precise Inference-Time Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines grounding-oriented reward and sampling improvements with inference-time image decomposition and target selection.

name: NaviMaster: Learning a Unified Policy for GUI and Embodied Navigation Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: NaviMaster trains a shared policy for GUI and embodied navigation using a common visual-trajectory formulation. It combines trajectory collection, reinforcement learning and distance-aware rewards, with evaluation across both task families.

name: MagicGUI: A Foundational Mobile GUI Agent with Scalable Data Pipeline and Reinforcement Fine-tuning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines a mobile GUI data pipeline, perception and planning capabilities, and reinforcement fine-tuning for interactive task execution.

name: Evolving in Tasks: Empowering the Multi-modality Large Language Model as the Computer Use Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Self-Evolution Agent combines automatic generation of verifiable computer-use trajectories with step-wise reinforcement learning for long-horizon training. It also describes a model-enhancement procedure that integrates grounding and planning capabilities without an additional training stage.

name: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces GuirlVG, an empirical study of reinforcement fine-tuning for GUI visual grounding. It analyzes training components and adds an adaptive KL-based mechanism to limit reward over-optimization.

name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

name: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding via Region Consistency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-RC aggregates multiple grounding predictions into spatial voting grids to choose a consensus region. GUI-RCPO then turns agreement with that region into a reward for test-time policy updates on unlabeled GUI screenshots.

name: InfiGUI-G1: Advancing GUI Grounding with Adaptive Exploration Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses multiple candidate answers and adaptive exploration rewards to improve spatial and semantic alignment in GUI grounding.

name: UI-Venus Technical Report: Building High-performance UI Agents with RFT
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Studies screenshot-based GUI grounding and navigation using curated interaction data, reward design, and reinforcement fine-tuning.

name: CRAFT-GUI: Curriculum-Reinforced Agent For GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CRAFT-GUI organizes GUI trajectories by difficulty for curriculum-based GRPO training. Its reward combines rule-based signals with model judgments, with evaluation on Android Control and an internal online benchmark.

name: ComputerRL: Scaling End-to-End Online Reinforcement Learning for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines API and GUI actions with distributed desktop reinforcement learning and alternating supervised training to address training instability.

name: InternVL3.5: Advancing Open-Source Multimodal Models in Versatility, Reasoning, and Efficiency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces InternVL3.5, a multimodal model family trained with Cascade RL and designed for more efficient inference; GUI interaction is among its stated capabilities.

name: InquireMobile: Teaching VLM-based Mobile Agent to Request Human Assistance via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: InquireMobile trains mobile agents to seek human confirmation at critical decisions using staged reinforcement fine-tuning and pre-action reasoning. InquireBench evaluates safe interaction and proactive inquiry, distinguishing asking for help from completing the underlying task.

name: SWIRL: A Staged Workflow for Interleaved Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract also applies SWIRL to mathematical reasoning; the GUI application is mobile control.
summary: Introduces SWIRL, staged interleaved RL for mobile GUI control, pairing a Navigator that plans from screens and language with an Interactor that produces actions.

name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.

name: UItron: Foundational GUI Agent with Advanced Perception and Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UItron combines GUI perception and planning data engineering with supervised training and curriculum reinforcement learning in connected mobile and PC environments. It also collects more than one million operation steps across 100 Chinese apps and builds offline and online evaluation environments.

name: Succeed or Learn Slowly: Sample Efficient Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Mobile App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Succeed or Learn Slowly applies direct off-policy updates to successful interactions and more conservative regularized updates to negative examples. Successful Transition Replay prioritizes successful experience during policy learning, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

name: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.

name: VeriOS: Query-Driven Proactive Human-Agent-GUI Interaction for Trustworthy OS Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces VeriOS-Agent, which learns when to execute GUI actions autonomously and when to query a user under untrustworthy conditions. Its staged training combines supervised learning and group-relative policy optimization.

name: UI-S1: Advancing GUI Automation via Semi-online Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-S1 simulates multi-turn online learning over offline trajectories, using a patch module to recover divergences while retaining the model’s own outputs in context. It combines discounted future returns with step- and episode-level advantages and introduces a semi-online performance proxy.

name: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces ReSum, which compresses interaction histories during long web searches, and ReSum-GRPO, which trains agents to reason across the resulting segments.

name: TGPO: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization for Robust Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TGPO merges semantically equivalent web states into tree-structured trajectories for offline preference optimization. A process reward model scores subgoal progress, redundant behavior, and action validity, while dynamic weighting emphasizes consequential decisions.

name: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-ARP uses visual attention to crop relevant screenshot regions and decides whether a target needs single-stage or multi-stage analysis. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO trains this adaptive procedure for high-resolution GUI grounding.

name: BTL-UI: Blink-Think-Link Reasoning Model for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.

name: Mano Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract reports evaluation on GUI benchmarks including Mind2Web and OSWorld.
summary: Introduces Mano, a GUI agent trained with simulated data, supervised fine-tuning, and offline and online RL, with a verification module for error recovery.

name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.

name: MobileRL: Online Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileRL adapts GRPO to mobile GUI training with difficulty-dependent replay of successes and filtering of failure curricula. A shortest-path reward adjustment accounts for task length, with evaluations on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces iStar, a general agentic RL method that learns implicit step rewards; WebShop is one of several interactive benchmarks used to evaluate it.

name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.

name: RISK: A Framework for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RISK combines browser-interaction training data, a benchmark, and reinforcement fine-tuning for e-commerce risk-management workflows. Its trajectories and rewards distinguish individual actions from multi-step stateful tasks involving deeply embedded web content.

name: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI agents provide testing feedback for generated websites; WebGen-Agent itself generates website code.
summary: Introduces WebGen-Agent for website code generation, using screenshot critiques and GUI-agent tests to refine code and provide step-level training rewards.

name: GUI-Shepherd: Reliable Process Reward and Verification for Long-Sequence GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces GUI-Shepherd, a process reward model trained on annotated GUI interactions to give step-level feedback for agent training and verification on AndroidWorld and AndroidControl.

name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.

name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.

name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.

name: Hi-Agent: Hierarchical Vision-Language Agents for Mobile Device Control
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. This Hi-Agent has a distinct author team and method from the earlier HiAgent working-memory paper; the shared project-name prefix is not treated as an identity match.
summary: Introduces Hi-Agent, jointly training a high-level reasoning model and a low-level mobile action model. Execution feedback supplies a foresight advantage for optimizing subgoal decisions, with evaluations on Android control benchmarks.

name: Agentic Entropy-Balanced Policy Optimization

name: UltraCUA: A Foundation Model for Computer Use Agents with Hybrid Action
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UI-Ins: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Multi-Perspective Instruction-as-Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: OpenPhone: Mobile Agentic Foundation Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.

name: GUI-Rise: Structured Reasoning and History Summarization for GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines structured progress-and-decision reasoning with history summarization to improve cross-domain generalization in GUI navigation agents.

name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.

name: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebArena is one of several environments used to evaluate this general agent training framework.

name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.

name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

name: Co-EPG: A Framework for Co-Evolution of Planning and Grounding in Autonomous GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.

name: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSGym supplies full operating-system sandboxes with GUIs for parallel computer-use data collection and training. It combines per-replica state management, hardware-aware orchestration, copy-on-write virtual-machine disks, and layered failure recovery.

name: STEP: Success-Rate-Aware Trajectory-Efficient Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: STEP allocates RL sampling by task success rate and trains on individual steps from interaction trajectories, with evaluations on OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

name: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work trains high-level schedulers with staged reinforcement learning driven by execution feedback. Its CES framework separates a Coordinator for planning and decomposition, a StateTracker for compressed context, and a low-level Executor.

notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: SmartSnap trains GUI agents to collect concise screenshot evidence of task completion for an LLM judge, with experiments on mobile tasks.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.

name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.

name: Computer Environments Elicit General Agentic Intelligence in LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: LLM-in-Sandbox gives agents a minimal computer environment for resource access, file management and code execution; LLM-in-Sandbox-RL trains models to use it.

name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.

name: Continual GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.

name: POINTS-GUI-G: GUI-Grounding Journey

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Code2World predicts future GUI screens through renderable code, trained on AndroidCode trajectories with supervised learning and render-aware reinforcement learning. It evaluates visual prediction and downstream AndroidWorld navigation with the learned world model.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).

name: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ADMIRE extracts milestones from successful GUI explorations to provide adaptive intermediate rewards. It assigns credit differently to successful and failed trajectories and evaluates training on AndroidWorld, with additional transfer studies in web and embodied settings.

name: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.

name: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.

name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebShop is one of the interactive benchmarks reported for this general agent-training method.

notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.

name: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: GUI-Libra trains GUI agents with action-aware supervision, a curated reasoning dataset and reinforcement learning adapted to partially verifiable actions across web and mobile tasks.

name: K^2-Agent: Co-Evolving Know-What and Know-How for Hierarchical Mobile Device Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces K2-Agent, a hierarchical mobile-control framework that refines task knowledge through a reasoning loop and trains an executor with curriculum-guided reinforcement learning.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as future work; this annotation does not assert current availability.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Training uses controllable virtual environments, and evaluation is reported on Memory-World.
